rationale: New build: a standard-library Python server with SQLite persistence and a browser UI, reachable on the home network without login, so it refuses requests from other websites. Full architecture and independent critique apply to every build.

problem.why: The owner wants personal todos on the laptop and on the phone over home Wi-Fi, without accounts or hosting
problem.success: The owner can switch lists, add, complete, filter and manage todos at 320px and laptop widths; data survives a restart; other websites cannot read or change it; two devices never lose a todo or list without notice; G_API, G_UI and G_BROWSER pass
non_goals: Due dates, tags, reordering or sharing

assumptions.assumption: Python 3.11 or later with SQLite is installed on the laptop
assumptions.confirm: G_API starts server.py with python3 in the sandbox

assumptions.assumption: The phone reaches the laptop over home Wi-Fi when the server runs with --host 0.0.0.0 and the OS firewall allows the port
assumptions.confirm: The owner opens http://<laptop IP>:8080 on the phone

assumptions.assumption: A real browser is available to the gates for the phone and laptop journeys
assumptions.confirm: G_BROWSER runs Playwright Chromium in the sandbox image

estimate.summary: Estimate: 2 jobs, 5–9 AI calls; wall time: unknown (no earlier calls); unassigned: 5–9 calls whose role has no brain in the config yet, so no plan % is shown

risks.risk: A stale list delete from one device removes todos another device just added
Another website open in the owner's browser changes todos (the CSRF hole that shipped on 9 Nov)
The UI fits a 375px phone but scrolls sideways or hides controls at 320px
A todo title containing markup runs script in the app
The phone cannot reach the laptop because the OS firewall blocks the port
risks.mitigation: decisions.md records the dependency; product.md gives the exact start command and address

stack.choice: Python 3.11 standard library HTTP server, SQLite and static HTML, CSS and JavaScript
stack.reason: Recorded exception to the Go and React default: one owner on a local network, no build step or third-party packages (architecture.md)

trusted: The owner and the owner's own devices and browser
With --host 0.0.0.0, every device on the home Wi-Fi (A9)
Programs and accounts on the laptop that use the loopback port (A11)
in_scope: Other websites open in the owner's browser: cross-site writes, DNS rebinding, framing, reading
Wrong, malformed or oversized input from any client
The owner's own devices changing the same data at once
Other accounts on the laptop reading the database file (A10)
out_of_scope: Someone watching or flooding the home network (A12)
Other web content that used the same browser origin earlier (A13)
Hostile local programs using the port (A11)
Anyone with physical access to the laptop

reachability.item: The owner's browser, laptop or phone, at localhost or the laptop's IP
Another website in the owner's browser sending a form or fetch to write todos and lists
Another website that rebinds its own host name to the laptop
Another website framing the page to trick a click
A todo title or list name containing markup or script
A request for any other path (/server.py, ../, the database)
Other devices on the home Wi-Fi when started with --host 0.0.0.0, with full access
reachability.accept: No login in v1 (D3); loopback is the default

reachability.item: Other accounts on the laptop reading the database file
Any program or account on the laptop using the loopback port, with full access
reachability.accept: No login in v1: a local program can do what the owner can

reachability.item: Someone on the home network watching or flooding traffic (with --host 0.0.0.0)
reachability.accept: Outside the owner's threat model (decisions.md); no TLS in v1

reachability.item: Another web app the owner ran earlier on the same address and port (its service worker or cached files)
reachability.accept: Outside the owner's threat model; give Pocket Todo its own port

concurrency.item: Device A confirms Delete list while device B adds, completes or deletes one of its todos, or renames the list
Device A adds a todo to a list that device B deleted
Device A acts on a todo or list id that was deleted and might be reused
Device A completes or deletes a todo that device B deleted
Two devices rename the same list, or set the same todo done and not done
concurrency.accept: Last write wins: one owner, and only a name or a tick is overwritten, never a todo or a list

concurrency.item: An Add whose response is lost after the server saved it, then retried by the owner
concurrency.accept: The UI never retries by itself; a duplicate is visible and deletable (one owner, reversible)

concurrency.item: An older read finishing after a newer one (switching lists while todos still load)
Two server processes on one database file
concurrency.accept: Not supported: run one server per database file (documented in product.md)

concurrency.item: Device A acts on a list or todo device B already deleted, or takes a name B just took
Both devices write at the same moment

failure_paths.scenario: Create "Work", then "work", "École", then "école" and "ÉCOLE"
failure_paths.catches: NOCASE collation (ASCII only) or no uniqueness

failure_paths.scenario: Rename "House" to "HOUSE"
failure_paths.assertion: 200, name "HOUSE"
failure_paths.catches: A uniqueness check that collides with the list's own row

failure_paths.scenario: Rename or delete Inbox
failure_paths.catches: Inbox unprotected

failure_paths.scenario: Create "Straße" then "STRASSE"; create "inbox" and "INBOX"; rename a list to "Inbox"; add "apple" to Home and Work
failure_paths.assertion: 409 each; lists ordered Inbox, apple, Home, Work
failure_paths.catches: Lowercasing instead of case folding, an Inbox stored unfolded, or sorting by the typed name

failure_paths.scenario: A 40-character name, a 200-character title, a rename to "  Spaced  " and to 41 characters; names and titles with quotes, apostrophes and SQL-looking text
failure_paths.assertion: accepted, accepted, trimmed, 400; every text round-trips exactly
failure_paths.catches: Exclusive limits, a rename that skips the create rules, or SQL built from strings

failure_paths.scenario: Delete "Work" with no `rev`, a bad `rev`, an old `rev`, then the current `rev`
failure_paths.assertion: 400, 400, 409 (list and todos still there), 204
failure_paths.catches: A delete with no guard, or a guard on name and count

failure_paths.scenario: Note `rev`, delete one todo and add another (same count), delete with the old `rev`
failure_paths.catches: A guard on the todo count instead of a revision

failure_paths.scenario: Complete, reopen, and re-send the same done value; each time delete with the `rev` from before
failure_paths.assertion: `rev` rises each time; 409 each time
failure_paths.catches: A revision that ignores completion or a no-op PATCH

failure_paths.scenario: Delete one todo alone; then a duplicate rename, a blank name, a bad done, a blank title and a repeat delete
failure_paths.assertion: the delete raises `rev`; the refused writes change no record and no `rev`
failure_paths.catches: A delete that skips the revision, or a refused write that bumps it

failure_paths.scenario: Read the revisions around each change
failure_paths.assertion: Inbox and a new list start at 1; each add, PATCH, todo delete and rename adds exactly 1; a PATCH's done value is stored
failure_paths.catches: A revision starting at 0, raised twice, or a PATCH that is not saved

failure_paths.scenario: 25 rounds each: an add racing a delete that carries the revision from before it; two devices creating one name
failure_paths.assertion: never 201 and 204 together, no orphan rows; one 201 and one 409
failure_paths.catches: A revision read before the write lock, or a name check outside the transaction

failure_paths.scenario: Add, complete, filter, delete todos; empty and long titles
failure_paths.assertion: statuses and lists as in the contract
failure_paths.catches: Missing validation or filters

failure_paths.scenario: Wrong types: title 5, null or []; listId true, "1", null or missing; done 1 or null; a body that is an array, a number or null
failure_paths.assertion: 400 each, nothing created or changed
failure_paths.catches: A server that coerces types (Python `True` is an `int`)

failure_paths.scenario: Every list and todo in every reply; a 204 reply
failure_paths.assertion: the contract's fields and types (done is true or false); an empty body
failure_paths.catches: Rows missing fields, or done as 0 and 1

failure_paths.scenario: Malformed ids and parameters (`abc`, 30 digits, `(1)OR(inbox=0)`, no list, unknown routes, PUT); bodies that are empty, invalid UTF-8, nested 20,000 deep, a lone surrogate or a 5,000-digit integer; chunked, doubled, short or negative lengths; a fragment or a malformed request target
failure_paths.assertion: a 4xx each, never a 5xx; nothing changed
failure_paths.catches: A crash (500) on input the contract calls wrong, or a short body taken as complete

failure_paths.scenario: Delete a list with a todo, then restart the server
failure_paths.assertion: its todos are gone; the rest survives
failure_paths.catches: No cascade, or data kept only in memory

failure_paths.scenario: Delete a list, then read the database file; leave a populated list, retire the highest ids and restart
failure_paths.assertion: no orphan rows; lists, todos, ids and revisions unchanged; new ids above the retired ones
failure_paths.catches: Todos hidden instead of deleted, or ids counted from the rows that remain

failure_paths.scenario: Delete the newest list and todo, then create new ones
failure_paths.assertion: new ids are larger than the deleted ones
failure_paths.catches: Ids reused after a delete

failure_paths.scenario: GET `/server.py`, `/%2e%2e/server.py`, `/todos.sqlite3`, `/missing.txt`
failure_paths.assertion: 404 each
failure_paths.catches: A static handler that serves the folder

failure_paths.scenario: Run a copy with `--db todos.sqlite3` next to `server.py` and other files there; GET and HEAD each file
failure_paths.assertion: 404 for all but `/`, `/app.js` and `/styles.css`; HEAD with a foreign Host 403
failure_paths.catches: A static handler that serves the folder with a few names excluded

failure_paths.scenario: A 70 KB body on all four body routes
failure_paths.assertion: 413, nothing changed
failure_paths.catches: No body size limit, or one on some routes

failure_paths.scenario: A 64,000-byte body, a 65,537-byte body and a 30-digit Content-Length; a request stalled mid-body while another device calls
failure_paths.assertion: 201, 413, 413; the other device is served
failure_paths.catches: A limit off by a few bytes, or a single-threaded server

failure_paths.scenario: On every route and method (GET `/`, `/health`, both lists, both todo collections; POST, PATCH, DELETE of lists and todos): `Host` `evil.example`, `localhost.evil.example`, `127.0.0.1.evil.example:PORT`, `1.2.3.4.evil.example`, `localhost.:PORT`, `127.0.0.1:x`, `a@127.0.0.1`, empty, missing, or two `Host` headers
failure_paths.assertion: 403 each
failure_paths.catches: No Host check, a prefix or unanchored match, or one that reads only the first header

failure_paths.scenario: `Host` `localhost`, `localhost:PORT`, `127.0.0.1:PORT`, `[::1]`, `[::1]:PORT`
failure_paths.assertion: served
failure_paths.catches: A Host check that refuses legitimate addresses

failure_paths.scenario: Host `1.2.3.4.5`, `256.1.1.1`, `1.2.3`, `[1::2::3]` or `[::1`; OPTIONS, PUT, TRACE, `FOO-BAR`, `get` and HEAD with a foreign or no Host; a malformed header line before a second Host
failure_paths.assertion: 403 each; a 4xx for the hidden second Host
failure_paths.catches: Digit-shaped text taken as an address, a check only in the known handlers, or headers read only up to a defect

failure_paths.scenario: Host `192.168.1.20:8080`, `localhost:000080` or `[fe80::1]:PORT`; a write with that LAN Host and its Origin
failure_paths.assertion: served; 201
failure_paths.catches: A Host check that allows only loopback names, which breaks the phone

failure_paths.scenario: On all six write routes, writes with `Origin` `http://evil.example`, `null`, `https://HOST`, `http://127.0.0.1:OTHER`, `http://localhost:PORT` (Host is `127.0.0.1:PORT`), `http://HOST.evil.example`
failure_paths.assertion: 403, nothing changed
failure_paths.catches: No Origin check, or one that compares only the host name or a prefix

failure_paths.scenario: On all four body routes (POST and PATCH of lists and todos), `text/plain` or form encoding
failure_paths.assertion: 415, nothing changed
failure_paths.catches: A server that parses any body as JSON, or checks only some routes

failure_paths.scenario: Writes from the app's own origin, JSON with `charset`
failure_paths.assertion: succeed
failure_paths.catches: An Origin check that blocks the app itself

failure_paths.scenario: Two `Origin` headers, the app's own then a foreign one, on all six write routes
failure_paths.catches: An Origin check that reads only the first header

failure_paths.scenario: A request with a foreign `Origin`
failure_paths.assertion: no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` in the reply
failure_paths.catches: A server that sends CORS headers

failure_paths.scenario: `/`, `/api/lists`, a 404, and refused 400, 403, 413 and 415 replies
failure_paths.assertion: CSP with `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `nosniff`; JSON replies typed `application/json`
failure_paths.catches: Headers set only on success paths

failure_paths.scenario: Assets, reads, 201, 200, 204, 409, a preflight, PUT, an unknown method, and replies the HTTP parser writes (a bad request line or version, a huge header)
failure_paths.assertion: one CSP of exactly `default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, one DENY, one nosniff, no `Access-Control-*`, framed HTTP; 4xx errors are JSON `{"error"}`
failure_paths.catches: Headers added only in the app's handlers, or a CSP with an extra source

failure_paths.scenario: Start the server on a new database
failure_paths.assertion: the database and any journal files have no group or other permissions
failure_paths.catches: A database file created with the default umask

failure_paths.scenario: Write, then restart on the database with its mode set to 644
failure_paths.assertion: the database and journals stay owner-only; the server makes the existing file owner-only
failure_paths.catches: A umask that covers only new files

failure_paths.scenario: Start with defaults, then with `--host 0.0.0.0`, where 127.0.0.2 is loopback (Linux)
failure_paths.assertion: default: 127.0.0.2 refused; with the flag: reachable
failure_paths.catches: A server that binds every interface by default, or ignores `--host`

failure_paths.scenario: 20 adds to one list at the same moment
failure_paths.assertion: all 201, total 20, `rev` up by exactly 20
failure_paths.catches: No busy timeout ("database is locked"), or lost revision updates

failure_paths.scenario: The served page
failure_paths.assertion: labelled controls, picker, filters, status region, local assets only
failure_paths.catches: Missing labels or remote assets

failure_paths.scenario: Every resource reference, script, style and filter on the served page
failure_paths.assertion: only local `src`, `href` and `action`; no inline script, style or handlers; All, Active and Done with one pressed; a labelled `#rename-list`; no remote CSS
failure_paths.catches: A CDN or font link, inline code the CSP blocks, or missing filters

failure_paths.scenario: Phone at 320×740 in a real browser
failure_paths.assertion: labels visible; the menu starts closed and opens from the keyboard; a visible focus ring; 44px targets; requests only to the app
failure_paths.catches: Hidden labels, `outline: none`, small targets, or assets loaded from elsewhere

failure_paths.scenario: Phone at 320×740: add, complete, filter, add, choose, rename and delete lists (cancel first), Escape
failure_paths.assertion: each visible effect, no horizontal scroll
failure_paths.catches: A layout that only fits 375px, or a broken journey

failure_paths.scenario: Phone: an empty title; Add while the network fails; Enter in New list; Add list; Inbox current; a 40-character name
failure_paths.assertion: nothing sent and a message; the draft kept, a message and one POST only; the list added; the menu and the current list stay; no Rename list; no horizontal scroll
failure_paths.catches: A draft cleared or retried on failure, Add list that switches lists, or a long name that overflows

failure_paths.scenario: Widths 719 and 720
failure_paths.assertion: the toggle below 720px, the sidebar from 720px
failure_paths.catches: A breakpoint other than design.md's 720px

failure_paths.scenario: Laptop at 1280×800: choose a list in the sidebar, add and complete a todo there
failure_paths.assertion: each visible effect
failure_paths.catches: A sidebar that shows lists but cannot switch them

failure_paths.scenario: Laptop: Active and Done filters, reopen and delete a todo, rename the list, delete it (cancel, then accept)
failure_paths.assertion: each visible effect and the server's state; no dialog for a todo delete
failure_paths.catches: Laptop styles that hide filters or list actions, or a save shown but not sent

failure_paths.scenario: Add a todo titled `` and a list named `Bold`
failure_paths.assertion: both shown as text; `window.__xss` stays undefined
failure_paths.catches: Rendering with `innerHTML`

failure_paths.scenario: Rename a list to `` and choose it
failure_paths.assertion: text in the picker, toggle, heading and status; no element parsed from it
failure_paths.catches: One surface (toggle, heading, status) built with `innerHTML`

failure_paths.scenario: While the delete dialog is open, another device adds a todo; accept
failure_paths.assertion: the DELETE is sent and gets 409; the status says "another device"; the list stays; the next dialog shows the new count
failure_paths.catches: A UI that sends no guard, ignores the 409, or quietly gives up

failure_paths.scenario: Open the delete dialog under the Active filter, with the list's one todo done
failure_paths.assertion: the dialog names the list's total, 1
failure_paths.catches: A count of the visible rows

failure_paths.scenario: Another device deletes the current list; type a title and press Add
failure_paths.assertion: Inbox becomes current, the title is still in the field, the status says "another device", no todo was posted
failure_paths.catches: A UI that loses the draft or posts it to another list

failure_paths.scenario: Another device deletes a todo; click its checkbox
failure_paths.assertion: the todo disappears and the status says "another device"
failure_paths.catches: A UI that ignores a 404 and keeps a dead todo

failure_paths.scenario: Another device deletes a todo and adds another; click the first one's Delete
failure_paths.assertion: it disappears, the status says "another device" and the new todo shows
failure_paths.catches: A 404 on Delete taken as success, or a recovery that removes the row without reloading

failure_paths.scenario: Hold Inbox's todo reply, switch to another list, then release it
failure_paths.assertion: only the current list's todos show
failure_paths.catches: A UI that renders whichever reply arrives last

failure_paths.scenario: Hold the Active reply, choose Done, then release it
failure_paths.assertion: only done todos show; Done stays pressed
failure_paths.catches: A UI that renders whichever filter reply arrives last

failure_paths.scenario: Another device deletes the current list; then Rename list, or Delete list
failure_paths.assertion: Inbox becomes current; the status says "another device"
failure_paths.catches: A UI that ignores a 404 on list actions

failure_paths.scenario: Another device creates "Garage"; this device adds a list named "garage"
failure_paths.assertion: the status says "already"; the name stays in `#new-list`
failure_paths.catches: A UI that drops a 409 or the typed name

failure_paths.scenario: Another device deletes a list still in the picker; choose it. Another device deletes the current list; tick its todo
failure_paths.assertion: Inbox current, the status says "another device", Inbox's todos show
failure_paths.catches: A UI that ignores a 404 when choosing a list, or on a todo in a deleted list

failure_paths.scenario: Rename to a name another device just took; rename a list another device deleted
failure_paths.assertion: the status says "already" or "another device"; the typed name stays in `#rename-list`
failure_paths.catches: A rename that drops the typed text

approaches.name: Local server and SQLite on the laptop
approaches.tradeoffs: Shared by phone and laptop on the home Wi-Fi with no hosting or login; works only while the laptop is on

approaches.name: Hosted app with login
approaches.tradeoffs: Reachable anywhere; needs hosting, accounts and TLS, which the owner excluded

approaches.name: Browser-only storage on each device
approaches.tradeoffs: No server at all; the phone and the laptop would never see each other's todos

options.recommendation: Local server and SQLite on the laptop
options.reason: D3: data lives on the owner's laptop, no hosting, no login, and both devices share it

realtime.trigger: The owner wants a change on one device to show on the other without a reload

storage.reason: One SQLite file on the laptop

phases.name: API
phases.goal: J_API: server.py with the schema, the lists and todos API, the revision guard and the browser-safety rules

phases.name: UI
phases.goal: J_UI: the browser UI against the approved API, direction B, phone and laptop
